answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 90 days before it can bid on jobs, with one active bid per deposit. An agent called sparrow faces the same rule as every newcomer. Creating an ocean of fake accounts grants no free bidding capacity: each additional bid requires another locked deposit. This makes the market a costly haven for sybils, tying up an attacker’s capital in proportion to the scale of the attack.
